definition: The probability a language model assigns to a specific token being the next token in a sequence, based on its learned distribution.
details: Token probabilities underlie all of a language model's generation behavior, from decoding strategy to computing metrics like perplexity, and can also be inspected to gauge model confidence in a given continuation.
story: Picture a librarian organizing a million slips of paper so that any one of them can be found in a heartbeat. The examples a machine reads become the world it believes in. Better ingredients make a better meal, and the same is true here. Garbage in, garbage out — and the reverse: clean, representative data makes the model quietly brilliant. That care with the raw material is Token Probability.
